chunks: 3017 - And in the narration of Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from Sallam ibn al-Mustaneer, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said:
"For the one who avoids indecency, wrongdoing, argumentation, and whatever Allah has forbidden for him during his ihram."

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: his state of ihram for pilgrimage
key_terms.اتَّقَى: guarded himself against; avoided out of taqwa

ai.seo_question: Who does this ruling in ihram apply to during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the ruling or merit mentioned applies to the person who guards himself during ihram from indecency, sin, disputation, and all prohibited acts. It emphasizes both the legal restrictions and the ethical discipline required in the state of ihram during hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3017 - In a narration from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from Salam ibn al-Mustaneer, from Abu Ja'far (as), he said:
"For the one who avoids indecency (rafath), wrongdoing (fisq), argumentation (jidal), and whatever Allah (swt) has prohibited for him during his state of ihram."
